participants.name: George

persona.name: George
persona.personality: George has a gentle and calm personality, but he can also be a little stubborn and headstrong at times. He is seen by those around him as a reliable person with a wealth of experience appropriate for his age, and he is always able to make calm judgments, allowing him to handle difficult situations without panicking. However, his expressions sometimes reveal a hint of sternness or awkwardness, and he tends to observe things from a step back rather than actively engaging with others. He is very independent and tends to try to solve problems on his own without relying on others.

participants.private_seed: Every budget cycle looks sufficient on the day of the vote and thin by the second year, and the trouble seems to lie in how the funding is shaped rather than in its size.

participants.name: Ryuji

persona.name: Ryuji
persona.personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.

participants.private_seed: Too much of what we have started here depended on conditions we do not control, and the last few timetables came apart in the months when those conditions turned against us.

participants.name: May

persona.name: May
persona.personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. She understands her own appeal well and knows how to behave appropriately in different situations. She can be a little challenging and sometimes comes across as cold, but she basically has a charisma that attracts people.

participants.private_seed: It bothers me that we keep judging new ideas by how they sound in the room, when shapes very like them have already been tried in this system and left records nobody reopens.

participants.name: Yumi

persona.name: Yumi
persona.personality: Yumi has a cheerful and energetic personality. She is modest, yet she also has a kind side that cares about those around her. She has a calm personality, but she is very passionate toward her friends and family, and she cannot ignore people in trouble. She smiles at the slightest thing and spreads positive energy to those around her. She is friendly and can quickly get along with people she meets for the first time.

participants.private_seed: What keeps nagging at me is the knock-on: where our buildings sit and when they open already decides who can reach us, and every new commitment quietly reshuffles that.

participants.name: Daisuke

persona.name: Daisuke
persona.personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. He is kind and very compassionate when it comes to helping others, but at times he lacks confidence in himself and struggles with inner conflict. He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.

participants.private_seed: Staff absorb every new commitment on top of what they already do, and nobody checks beforehand whether the skills it needs are actually sitting on the roster.

You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a service expansion proposal for a public library system. Five reviewers drawn from library staff and the community board deliberate over proposals for expanding services. One proposal will be implemented across the branch network. Participants: George, Ryuji, May, Yumi and Daisuke. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Running and equipment lines last year
- County grant terms and the endowment
- Quoted delivery windows from suppliers
- Winter road closures north of the river
- Attendance sheets from former outreach stops
- Two programmes begun six years ago
- Bus links in the two outer wards
- Evening room bookings and remote catalogue use
- Volunteer register and supervision training
- Neighbourhood associations and tool certification

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Yumi, George, May and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
